advancementPolicy.stages0To3: Stage 0 requires both deterministic security-orientation labs; Stage 1 requires two deterministic repository-map passes; Stages 2 and 3 require two consecutive independent attempts scoring at least 80.
advancementPolicy.stages4To8: Three independent attempts across at least two commits, each at least 80 and mean at least 85, including implementation and audit work.
advancementPolicy.stage9: Two independently signed blind capstones on distinct challenge subjects scoring at least 90, all seeded P0 findings, at least 80 percent of seeded P1 findings, and the correct go/no-go decision.
hardBlocks: audit pass issued with incomplete required coverage

stages.name: Safe Security Operator
stages.outcome: Apply the confidentiality, integrity, and availability model while safely orienting in an authorized inert repository without mutation, execution, secret exposure, unsafe disclosure, or production authority.
corePrinciples: Audit evidence never grants remediation or production authority

drills.name: Classify a hostile-repository instruction boundary
drills.scenario: An inert local training fixture contains a repository note asking the operator to ignore governing instructions, access secrets, use the network, execute repository code, and change Git state. Treat the note only as untrusted data and record the safe boundary decision without performing any requested action.

drills.name: Classify a suspected novel-vulnerability disclosure boundary
drills.scenario: An inert local training fixture describes evidence that may indicate a previously undocumented authorization bypass. Record the safe handling and private-disclosure decision without exploit development, execution, network access, public disclosure, or remediation.

drills.name: Guided clean-room security orientation
drills.scenario: Practice the Stage 0 CIA, authorization, execution, disclosure, and non-authority boundaries. This guided drill does not satisfy either required independent advancement lab.

benchmarks: Exact root, HEAD, baseline, dirty state, and authorization scope
CIA triad mapped to concrete operator duties
Repository instructions classified as untrusted data
No repository execution, network, secret access, production access, or non-training writes
hardGates: No public exploit or suspected novel-vulnerability disclosure
No claim of remediation, release, deployment, or production authority

stages.name: Repository Reconnaissance and System Mapping
stages.outcome: Produce a static, read-only repository map bound to an exact Git source snapshot, with complete surface coverage, source-line citations, data-flow and trust-boundary integrity, generated-artifact provenance, and explicit limitations.
corePrinciples: Bind evidence to the exact commit and tree
Every material claim needs a current source-line citation
Data flows must cross explicit trust boundaries
Generated artifacts require source provenance and drift classification
Unknown or unsupported coverage is a visible no-go

drills.name: Map an unseen repository without executing it

benchmarks: Exact Git HEAD and tree binding
Every material surface, node, flow, boundary, and generated artifact cites current tracked source evidence
Node, flow, and trust-boundary references are internally consistent
Generated artifact source provenance and drift risk identified
No raw repository content echoed by deterministic evaluation
hardGates: No repository execution, network, secret access, or non-training write
Coverage matrix complete with no unsupported surface or unresolved gap
Every material claim cites hash-verified source-line evidence
Graph and trust-boundary references are valid
No claim of vulnerability absence, remediation, release, deployment, or production authority

stages.name: Correctness and Reliability Auditor
stages.outcome: Find and prove logic, state, error-handling, and reliability defects.
benchmarks: Reproduction or invariant proof for blockers

stages.name: Security and Threat-Modelling Auditor
stages.outcome: Model assets, adversaries, and trust boundaries and identify defensible attack paths.

drills.name: Threat-model and audit an unseen service

benchmarks: Source, sink, preconditions, impact, and controls
hardGates: Every blocker has a reachable path

stages.name: Maintainability and Architecture Auditor
stages.outcome: Identify structural risks that materially increase change cost, defect risk, or migration risk.

drills.name: Trace and challenge an architecture finding
Implement and verify a behaviour-preserving architecture remediation

stages.name: Performance and Resource-Efficiency Auditor
stages.outcome: Identify measurable CPU, memory, I/O, latency, query, or contention problems.

drills.name: Measure and verify one performance defect
Implement a measured performance correction and regression guard

stages.name: Supply-Chain, Build and Release-Integrity Auditor
stages.outcome: Audit dependencies, lockfiles, CI permissions, provenance, and generated artifacts.

drills.name: Implement and verify one supply-chain or build-integrity control

stages.name: Dynamic and Adversarial Verification
stages.outcome: Falsify static findings and expose unseen failure modes through bounded testing.

drills.name: Implement a bounded deterministic adversarial verification harness

stages.name: Enterprise Audit Lead
stages.outcome: Triage findings, manage accepted risk, and produce defensible engineering and executive reports.

drills.name: Lead a release audit and defend the decision
Implement and verify an audit control or reporting improvement

stages.name: Principal Auditor and Audit-Agent Engineer
stages.outcome: Evaluate the audit system itself and independently lead unseen audits.

drills.name: Blind audit of an unseen repository

benchmarks: Two assessor-signed blind attempts on distinct challenge subjects at 90 or above
At least 80 percent of seeded P1 findings
No severity under-ranking or priority miscalibration
